episode_title: Why Sacramento’s Next Decade Could Be Its Biggest Yet | Bryan Flaherty

real_qa.q: Why is Sacramento Business Journal one of only three growing national business news publications, and how did the decision to charge for internet content from day one contribute to this growth?
real_qa.r: We made a great bet back in mid-2015, 2014 when the internet was becoming everything for news. A lot of folks continued to charge for their product and make their internet content free, but we said what's the difference—we're charging for internet content from day one. Our colleagues and friends had a hard time putting that toothpaste back in the tube, but we didn't necessarily have to. That was a great bet that we made. We are one of three business news organizations that are growing—us, The Wall Street Journal, and The New York Times—and we're not doing it through acquisition. We are doing it just purely based on subscription growth and marketing growth.
real_qa.requete: Sacramento Business Journal growth subscription strategy

real_qa.q: How many Business Journal markets does Advanced Publications operate, and what is the difference in coverage between markets with publishers versus digital-only markets?
real_qa.r: There are 46 now. We actually just opened Fort Worth Business Journal. Currently we have 40 journals that have publisher and events. When you have a publisher in events, you do have a little bit more—your market share and your impact is much greater. The digital-only markets that we have are sometimes smaller markets. LA, New York, Chicago, we only have a digital market because those newspapers and those legacy journals really dominate there.

guest.bio_context: Bryan Flaherty has been in the media industry for 11 years and recently became the new publisher and market president of the Sacramento Business Journal, succeeding David Lickman. He moved to Sacramento in 2020 with his wife Molly after living in Portland, Oregon, where he worked in media buying for local TV and radio before transitioning to the sales side at the Portland Business Journal. Both he and his wife studied journalism at the University of Oregon and discovered they had remarkably parallel lives—same age, same major, lived in the same dorm, birthdays a day apart, and both born in the Sacramento region.

real_quote: When we have to make another bet when it comes to the change in how news is produced and how news is consumed, we're on the right side of that again.
